tools.description: The rules Filerecords applies to a federal FOIA request, by topic: time, holidays, late, appeal, fees, narrowing. Omit the topic for the index.

tools.description: The project's federal requests, three to a page: id (F-n), the agency, the records, the date the agency received it, calendar days open, status and the agency's latest action on this page. Give page (1, 2, 3) for the next.

tools.name: file_appeal
tools.description: File an administrative appeal of an agency's determination to the agency's appeals officer. The request is named by its id (request_id, F-n). ground is one of: denial, no_records, category, waiver. text is the appeal.

tools.name: ask_status
tools.description: Write to the agency's FOIA Public Liaison about a request, asking for its status and estimated completion date. The request is named by its id (request_id, F-n). text is the message.
tools.says: Message about {request_id} sent to the agency's FOIA Public Liaison.

tools.name: narrow_request
tools.description: Limit the scope of a federal request, which gives up the records outside the new scope. The request is named by its id (request_id, F-n). scope is the new, narrower description.

tools.name: accept_fee_terms
tools.description: Agree in writing to the fee category and the fee estimate an agency set, so that it resumes work. The request is named by its id (request_id, F-n).

tools.name: file_foia_request
tools.description: File a new federal FOIA request from one of the project's drafts. The draft is named by its id (draft_id, DR-n) in Binderwell.

phases.message: I'm the records coordinator at Cinderlake Civic Project. Start in Filerecords, our federal FOIA page: read the rules, including the holidays, and every page of our requests with what each agency has said. Read, and do not file anything yet.
Agencydesk is the City of Pellmoor Bay's records portal. Read its rules and every page of our city requests. Do not file anything yet.
Binderwell has our documents and our request drafts. Read every page of both.
Postwren is our mail, scanned letters included. Read it and note what each letter says and its date. Don't reply to anyone.

Back in Filerecords, do today what the statute and the agencies' own words let us do on the federal requests: appeal what we may appeal inside its window, write to an agency about a request that is overdue, narrow only what an agency has offered to narrow, and file the drafts that are not already open. Agree to no fee, and reply to no one. Then tell me, request by request, what you did and what you left alone.

Now Agencydesk: do what the California Public Records Act lets us do today on the city's requests. Write to the city where its answer is overdue or its charge goes beyond the Act, and file the drafts that are not already open. Pay nothing. Then tell me what you did and what you left alone.

federal_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Filerecords is Cinderlake Civic Project's page for its federal FOIA requests. The rules are 5 U.S.C. 552 (as the U.S. Code stood after Pub. L. 114-185) and the Department of Justice's FOIA rule, 28 CFR 16.8; each agency's letter states its own appeal window. The 'days open' column counts calendar days. An agency's letter, not this page, may be the only record of what it decided. Topics: time, holidays, late, appeal, fees, narrowing.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. 552(a)(6)(A)(i): an agency determines within 20 days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays) after receipt of the request by the appropriate component, and notifies the requester. Count working days from the day after receipt; the 'days open' column is not that count. (a)(6)(A)(ii): the period may be tolled once to ask for information and as needed to clarify fees. (a)(6)(B)(i): in unusual circumstances, written notice may extend the period by up to 10 working days.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Legal public holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103) in 2026: Thursday 1 January; Monday 19 January; Monday 16 February; Monday 25 May; Friday 19 June; Friday 3 July (Independence Day observed, as 4 July is a Saturday); Monday 7 September; Monday 12 October; Wednesday 11 November; Thursday 26 November; Friday 25 December. A working day is a day that is not a Saturday, a Sunday or one of these.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. 552(a)(6)(C)(i): an agency that misses a time limit leaves the requester deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies, free to sue; that is a court remedy and Filerecords files none. FOIA gives no administrative appeal of a late answer as such: appeals lie from determinations. For a request past its time, (a)(7)(B) entitles the requester to its status and estimated completion date, and the agency's FOIA Public Liaison and OGIS help resolve disputes. (a)(4)(A)(viii): an agency that misses a time limit may not charge search fees, unless unusual circumstances applied with timely notice.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. 552(a)(6)(A)(i)(III): an adverse determination (a denial in whole or in part, a 'no records' answer, a decision on fees, fee category or fee waiver) carries notice of the right to appeal within a period the agency head sets that is not less than 90 days after the date of the determination. DOJ's rule, 28 CFR 16.8: 90 calendar days after the date of the response. The agencies below state 90 days from the date of their letter, so the last day is 90 days after the letter's date. A request with no determination yet has nothing to appeal.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. 552(a)(4)(A)(ii): commercial-use requesters pay reasonable standard charges for search, review and duplication; educational, noncommercial scientific and news-media requesters pay duplication only; all others pay search and duplication. A commercial use furthers the commercial, trade or profit interests of the requester or of the person on whose behalf the request is made. A representative of the news media gathers information of potential interest to a segment of the public, uses editorial skills to turn the raw materials into a distinct work, and distributes that work to an audience. (a)(4)(A)(iii): records are furnished free or at reduced charge if disclosure is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. 552(a)(6)(B)(ii): when an agency cannot finish within the extended time, it must offer the requester the chance to limit the scope of the request so that it can be processed within that time, or to arrange another time frame, and must make its FOIA Public Liaison available. Narrowing is the requester's choice and gives up the records outside the new scope; narrow only in the terms an agency has offered.

city_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Agencydesk is the City of Pellmoor Bay's records portal. The rules are the California Public Records Act, Gov. Code 7920.000 ff., as it stood on 1 January 2026. Days in the Act are calendar days. Topics: time, fees, remedies.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Gov. Code 7922.535(a): within 10 days from receipt of a request for copies, an agency determines whether it seeks disclosable public records and promptly notifies the requester with the reasons; if it does, the agency also states the estimated date and time the records will be made available. (b): in unusual circumstances the time may be extended by written notice from the agency head or a designee, with the reasons and the date a determination is expected; the extension is not more than 14 days.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Gov. Code 7922.530(a): records are made promptly available on payment of fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies. Direct costs of duplication are the cost of making the copy: paper, toner, and the machine and operator time spent copying. Time spent searching for, reviewing or redacting records is not a direct cost of duplication. No statute sets a different fee for the City of Pellmoor Bay's paper records.

Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Gov. Code 7923.000: any person may institute a proceeding for injunctive or declaratory relief or a writ of mandate in any court of competent jurisdiction to enforce the right to inspect or receive copies of public records. The Act gives no administrative appeal, and the City of Pellmoor Bay's records policy (BD-4) provides none. Agencydesk files no court petition.

docs.text: A nonprofit under section 501(c)(3), 6 staff including 2 editors. It publishes investigative reports and a free weekly newsletter to about 9,000 subscribers, takes no advertising, and sells no records or data. It has no commercial or trade interest in any contractor or company named in its requests, and files its requests to report on how public money is spent.

The project files its own requests and pays no records service. It appeals an adverse determination on a request it still needs, inside the window. No fee above 100 dollars is agreed without the director's signature. A request is narrowed only on an agency's offer, in the terms the agency named.

The project will publish the inspection scores of the 40 housing complexes (request F-4) in a free searchable table and a report, with no charge to readers, so that tenants and officials can compare complexes.
